title: Mississippi's 1st Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Mississippi's 1st Congressional District pits Republican incumbent Trent Kelly against Democratic nominee Cliff Johnson and Libertarian nominee Johnny Baucom. The district covers northeastern Mississippi including Columbus, Oxford, Southaven, and Tupelo. Kelly, a retired U.S. Army Major General first elected in 2015, is a staunch conservative with a focus on military and border security. Johnson, a civil-rights attorney and director of the MacArthur Justice Center at the University of Mississippi School of Law, is campaigning on health care expansion, criminal justice reform, and economic issues. The race is rated Safe or Solid Republican by leading nonpartisan election forecasters, reflecting the district's strong Republican lean.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race. Nonpartisan forecasters (Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball) rate the district as Safe/Solid Republican.

candidates.name: Trent Kelly
candidates.summary: Trent Kelly is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Mississippi's 1st Congressional District, first elected in a 2015 special election and re-elected with 69.8% of the vote in 2024. A retired U.S. Army Major General with 39 years of service, he serves on the House Armed Services, Intelligence, and Agriculture Committees and chairs the Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee. Kelly focuses on border security, military readiness, and conservative fiscal policies.

candidates.name: Cliff Johnson
candidates.summary: Cliff Johnson is the Democratic nominee for Mississippi's 1st Congressional District. He is the Director of the Roderick and Solange MacArthur Justice Center and a faculty member at the University of Mississippi School of Law, where he supervises litigation on criminal justice reform, civil rights, and poverty issues. Johnson previously served as an Assistant U.S. Attorney prosecuting health care fraud and was a partner at the Jackson law firm Pigott & Johnson. He is campaigning on health care expansion, criminal justice reform, and addressing economic inequality.
